articles.title: Natal Sicoob Credisul terá neve, presépio e chegada do Papai Noel em Vilhena  | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação gratuita começa em 14 de novembro, às 18h30, com atrações para toda a família, distribuição de pipoca e algodão-doce e visitação à Casa do Papai Noel
articles.summary: Programação gratuita começa em 14 de novembro, às 18h30, com atrações para toda a família, distribuição de pipoca e algodão-doce e visitação à Casa do Papai Noel
articles.body:
Natal Sicoob Credisul terá neve, presépio e chegada do Papai Noel em Vilhena — Foto: Divulgação

O Natal é tempo de encontros, de reunir a família e de criar lembranças que ficam na memória. É com esse espírito e com o tema “O Melhor Presente é Pertencer” que a Sicoob Credisul abre sua programação natalina em Vilhena, no dia 14 de novembro, às 18h30. A noite terá o acender das luzes, um presépio em tamanho real, que receberá a bênção de um padre e a chegada do Papai Noel e suas duendes com muita neve. A entrada será gratuita e aberta a toda a população, no CTC Sicoob Credisul, localizado na Avenida Capitão Castro, 3112, ao lado da Escola Wilson Camargo. Também haverá distribuição gratuita de pipoca e algodão-doce para os visitantes.

Depois da abertura, a Casa do Papai Noel ficará aberta à visitação até 23 de dezembro, de quarta a domingo, das 17h30 às 21h. O bom velhinho e suas duendes estarão no local para receber as famílias, conversar com as crianças e tirar fotos, proporcionando momentos de proximidade e diversão para quem visitar o espaço.

O presépio em tamanho real será um dos destaques da decoração natalina. A representação da cena do nascimento de Jesus resgata uma das tradições mais conhecidas do Natal cristão e integra o cenário preparado para receber a comunidade.

A Feira das Coisas – Hub de Economia Circular, também entra no clima natalino com uma edição especial. Por lá, o público poderá encontrar artigos variados, conhecer o trabalho dos expositores e descobrir opções de presentes para este Natal. A feira acontece no CTC Sicoob Credisul até 23 de dezembro, às sextas-feiras, sábados e domingos, das 17h às 21h.

“O Melhor Presente é Pertencer” é um convite a olhar com mais atenção para o que realmente tem valor na vida. Pertencer é sentir-se acolhido, saber que existe espaço para ser quem somos e ter pessoas com quem dividir os momentos bons e difíceis. É reconhecer que os vínculos que criamos, a confiança que compartilhamos e a presença de quem caminha ao nosso lado tornam a vida mais significativa.

Essa mensagem também encontra sentido no cooperativismo, que valoriza a participação de cada pessoa e entende que a força de uma cooperativa está justamente em quem faz parte dela. Na Sicoob Credisul, esse princípio se expressa na relação com os cooperados e no trabalho desenvolvido para gerar oportunidades e contribuir com as comunidades onde está presente.

Neste Natal, o tema nos lembra que pertencer também é participar, contribuir e saber que temos um lugar nessa construção.

articles.title: Balança comercial tem superávit de US$ 9,3 bilhões em outubro, alta de 39,4% | G1
articles.standfirst: No acumulado dos dez primeiros meses deste ano, o saldo positivo da balança comercial alcança US$ 71,04 bilhões, informou o MDIC. Exportações para os EUA quase dobraram.
articles.summary: No acumulado dos dez primeiros meses deste ano, o saldo positivo da balança comercial alcança US$ 71,04 bilhões, informou o MDIC. Exportações para os EUA quase dobraram.
articles.body:
A balança comercial brasileira registrou um superávit de US$ 9,318 bilhões no mês de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Sandro Menezes/governo do RN

A balança comercial brasileira registrou um superávit de US$ 9,318 bilhões no mês de outubro de 2026 , segundo dados divulgados pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC).

O resultado representa uma alta de 39,4% em comparação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando o saldo positivo havia ficado em US$ 6,68 bilhões.

🔎 O superávit comercial ocorre quando o valor total das exportações supera o das importações no período. Quando as compras no exterior superam as vendas, o resultado da balança é deficitário.

as exportações somaram US$ 37,807 bilhões, um crescimento de 20,0% em relação a outubro de 2025;

as importações totalizaram US$ 28,490 bilhões, com expansão de 14,8% na mesma comparação;

a corrente de comércio, somando todas as movimentações, alcançou US$ 66,297 bilhões, registrando uma alta de 17,7%.

Destaques dos produtos exportados pelo Brasil

Segundo Herlon Brandão, diretor de Estatísticas e Estudos de Comércio Exterior do MDIC, o crescimento das exportações foi concentrado em alguns produtos, principalmente combustíveis.

“No petróleo bruto tivemos um crescimento de US$ 195 milhões em outubro do ano passado para US$ 1,3 bilhão” neste ano, afirmou.

Segundo ele, mais da metade do aumento das vendas para os Estados Unidos veio desse produto. Brandão também citou os óleos combustíveis e a carne bovina entre os itens que contribuíram para o resultado.

Óleos brutos de petróleo: registraram forte expansão de 122,6%, somando um acréscimo de US$ 4,70 bilhões nas vendas do mês;

Óleos combustíveis de petróleo (exceto brutos): registraram salto de 164,5%, com avanço de US$ 1,12 bilhão;

Centeio, aveia e outros cereais não moídos: apresentaram crescimento expressivo na agropecuária, com aumento de US$ 0,34 bilhão;

Farelos de soja e alimentos para animais: subiram 39,1%, adicionando US$ 0,30 bilhão;

Soja em grão: teve crescimento de 8,9%, somando US$ 0,26 bilhão a mais do que em outubro do ano anterior;

Celulose: teve alta de 25,8%, agregando US$ 0,21 bilhão às exportações.

No recorte por setores econômicos nas exportações, a Indústria Extrativa liderou os ganhos com alta de 53,5% (totalizando US$ 11,52 bilhões) , seguida pela Agropecuária (+12,8%) e pela Indústria de Transformação (+7,7%).

Desempenho nos principais mercados compradores

A relação comercial com os principais parceiros do Brasil apresentou movimentações relevantes em outubro:

Estados Unidos: as exportações brasileiras para o mercado americano dispararam 87,0%, atingindo US$ 4,32 bilhões (aumento absoluto de US$ 2,01 bilhões ), impulsionadas por petróleo e carne bovina. As importações vindas dos EUA subiram 28,6%, para US$ 5,10 bilhões.

União Europeia: o bloco europeu registrou aumento de 32,0% nas exportações brasileiras, alcançando US$ 6,04 bilhões. As importações de produtos da União Europeia cresceram 8,0%, somando US$ 4,70 bilhões, levando a corrente de comércio com o bloco a US$ 10,74 bilhões (alta de 20,3%).

China: as exportações para o mercado chinês recuaram 5,3% em outubro, totalizando US$ 8,59 bilhões (frente aos US$ 9,07 bilhões registrados em outubro de 2025). Em contrapartida, as importações brasileiras de produtos chineses subiram 17,1%, atingindo US$ 7,53 bilhões.

Apesar do avanço, Brandão ponderou que ainda não é possível afirmar que os efeitos do tarifaço imposto por Donald Trump tenham sido superados.

Donald Trump anuncia tarifas em julho — Foto: AFP

No acumulado dos dez primeiros meses de 2026, a balança comercial brasileira registra saldo positivo acumulado de US$ 71,04 bilhões, um avanço de 34,1% na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior.

Exportações acumuladas: US$ 321,884 bilhões, crescimento de 11,2%.

Importações acumuladas: US$ 250,844 bilhões, alta de 6,1%.

Corrente de comércio acumulada: US$ 572,728 bilhões, expansão de 8,9%.

articles.title: Golpe do banco extinto: Operação Lázaro mira fraude de R$ 2 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Dez mandados de busca e apreensão forma cumpridos em residências de alto padrão no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.summary: O golpe do banco extinto visava cobrar uma dívida bilionária do governo através de precatórios, resultando em mandados de busca em imóveis de luxo no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
Oito pessoas foram indiciadas por suspeita de participar de um esquema criminoso que tentou reativar um banco extinto há mais de 60 anos para reivindicar uma dívida do governo que poderia chegar a R$ 2 bilhões.

A investigação aponta que o grupo teria se passado por acionistas da instituição e contado com a suposta colaboração de servidores públicos para conseguir o registro da reativação.

Nesta sexta-feira (6), a polícia cumpriu dez mandados de busca e apreensão em imóveis de alto padrão nas zonas Sul e Sudoeste do Rio. Na casa de um dos investigados, foram apreendidos quase R$ 100 mil em dinheiro, além de euros e dólares.

A investigação faz parte da segunda fase da Operação Lázaro, que apura suspeitas de falsidade ideológica, estelionato, corrupção e associação criminosa.

Polícia investiga tentativa de reativar banco extinto há mais de 60 anos para aplicar golpe bilionário — Foto: Reprodução

Banco extinto em 1964 foi reativado na Junta Comercial

O Banco de Crédito Móvel (BCM) deixou de existir em 1964. Segundo a investigação, cerca de seis décadas depois, integrantes do grupo se apresentaram como acionistas para tentar reativar a instituição.

O procedimento foi realizado na Junta Comercial do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Jucerja), com a suposta participação de servidores públicos. De acordo com a polícia, os funcionários teriam recebido promessas de pagamento que somavam R$ 600 mil para facilitar o processo.

Grupo pretendia reivindicar precatório de terreno no Recreio

Segundo a polícia, o objetivo da reativação era reivindicar um precatório relacionado à desapropriação de um terreno de 153 mil metros quadrados no Recreio dos Bandeirantes, na Zona Sudoeste do Rio.

Objetivo da reativação era reivindicar um precatório relacionado à desapropriação de um terreno — Foto: Reprodução

Precatório é uma dívida que o poder público tem que pagar após uma decisão judicial definitiva. A suspeita é que o grupo pretendia se apropriar do valor, que poderia chegar a R$ 2 bilhões.

As investigações também identificaram indícios de envolvimento dos suspeitos em fraudes imobiliárias, invasões de terrenos e empreendimentos irregulares na Barra da Tijuca.

Quatro investigados terão que usar tornozeleira eletrônica

A Justiça determinou medidas cautelares contra quatro investigados. Eles deverão usar tornozeleira eletrônica e cumprir recolhimento domiciliar durante a noite.

A reportagem procurou a Junta Comercial do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, mas não recebeu resposta até a última atualização. Também não conseguiu contato com as defesas dos investigados.

articles.title: Paraguai começa a devolver dinheiro a clientes de banco em crise | G1
articles.body:
O B anco Central do Paraguai começou a pagar na tarde de quinta-feira (5) os primeiros valores a clientes do Ueno Bank , cuja intervenção deixou cerca de 3 milhões de correntistas sem acesso ao dinheiro e provocou uma crise política no país.

A entidade publicou uma página explicando como funciona o resgate dos montantes e como consultar os pagamentos .

A informação foi confirmada nesta sexta-feira (6) à agência AFP por José Maciel , diretor da Unidade Administradora do Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos (FGD) do Banco Central paraguaio. O fundo é responsável por garantir a devolução de depósitos aos clientes de instituições financeiras, dentro dos limites previstos em lei.

"O processo de pagamento dos adiantamentos da garantia aos correntistas do Ueno Bank começou na tarde desta quinta-feira", afirmou Maciel à AFP.

De acordo com comunicado publicado pelo Banco Central, a primeira etapa contempla clientes que tenham até R$ 8,9 mil depositados no banco , não possuam dívidas com a instituição e tenham uma conta habilitada em outra instituição financeira do país .

O órgão informou que os correntistas que tenham até os R$ 8,9 mil em depósitos receberão a totalidade dos valores . Os pagamentos aos demais grupos serão anunciados posteriormente, conforme o andamento do processo e dentro do prazo previsto na legislação.

O Banco Central também esclareceu que pessoas físicas e jurídicas vinculadas ao Ueno Bank não têm direito à cobertura do fundo , conforme a Lei nº 2.334/2003. Caso recebam algum valor, deverão devolvê-lo ao fundo em até 24 horas, sem prejuízo de eventuais medidas judiciais.

Entenda a crise financeira do Paraguai que levou à renúncia do Presidente

O Ueno Bank, maior banco digital do Paraguai e principal emissor de cartões de crédito do país, enfrenta problemas financeiros e é alvo de investigações.

A instituição tem cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e passou por uma intervenção do Banco Central paraguaio, que interrompeu o acesso dos correntistas ao dinheiro depositado.

A situação se agravou depois que ajustes nos balanços do banco fizeram seu índice de solvência — indicador que mede a capacidade de uma instituição financeira de cumprir suas obrigações — cair para menos da metade do mínimo exigido pela regulamentação.

Diante do risco, o Banco Central iniciou um procedimento para proteger os depositantes e evitar que os problemas atingissem outras instituições financeiras. O Ministério Público também pediu a abertura de uma investigação criminal e determinou a prisão de oito pessoas ligadas ao banco. Ao todo, 27 pessoas são investigadas por suspeita de fraude e estelionato.

Nos meses anteriores à crise, o Ueno já estava sob maior fiscalização. Os órgãos reguladores investigavam se a instituição havia financiado indiretamente a venda de uma carteira de ativos de uma empresa ligada ao Grupo Vázquez, seu controlador. O banco negava ter participado da operação.

O caso também ganhou dimensão política. Carlos Carvallo, que presidia o Banco Central e havia comandado o próprio Ueno até agosto de 2023, renunciou ao cargo na terça-feira (3), em meio às críticas sobre a fiscalização da instituição. O presidente Santiago Peña, que foi sócio do grupo controlador do banco até março de 2025, também passou a enfrentar pressão.

A crise provocou protestos de clientes que foram às agências e encontraram as portas fechadas. Entre os afetados estão aposentados que recebem benefícios do governo por meio do banco. O Ueno administra aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em recursos públicos, incluindo valores do Instituto de Previsão Social (IPS), responsável pelo pagamento de aposentadorias e pensões no país.

Diante da situação, Peña anunciou um acordo com lideranças do Congresso para acelerar a votação de um projeto que autorizasse o uso do Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos para ressarcir os clientes. O mecanismo funciona como uma proteção para quem mantém dinheiro em instituições financeiras: em determinadas situações, o fundo é utilizado para devolver os valores depositados, respeitando os limites previstos em lei.

O presidente também afirmou que a medida deveria assegurar a devolução de recursos públicos mantidos pelo IPS e por outros fundos de previdência.

O Banco Central e Peña afirmaram que o caso é isolado e não representa um problema generalizado no sistema financeiro paraguaio. Segundo o presidente, trata-se de uma situação específica de uma instituição. A Superintendência de Bancos também anunciou que nomearia auditores para verificar os ativos do Ueno.

A crise teve reflexos no mercado financeiro e pressionou tanto os títulos em dólar emitidos pelo banco quanto os papéis da dívida pública do Paraguai. O episódio também levantou preocupações sobre a imagem do país como destino de investimentos estrangeiros, especialmente de capital brasileiro.

* Reportagem em atualização. Com informações da AFP.

O Ueno Bank é o principal emissor de cartões de crédito do Paraguai — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

articles.title: Usuários reclamam de PIX fora do ar; BC diz que falha foi resolvida | G1
articles.standfirst: Clientes apontaram falhas em aplicativos e transferências de instituições como Itaú, Bradesco, Santander, Nubank e Inter. Banco Central disse que sistema teve uma indisponibilidade parcial.
articles.summary: Clientes apontaram falhas em aplicativos e transferências de instituições como Itaú, Bradesco, Santander, Nubank e Inter. Banco Central disse que sistema teve uma indisponibilidade
articles.body:
Polícia mapeou valor do prejuízo após analisar transferências via PIX do suspeito — Foto: Bruno Peres/Agência Brasil/Arquivo

Usuários tiveram dificuldades para fazer transferências por PIX no início da noite desta sexta-feira (6). As reclamações começaram por volta das 19h, segundo o Downdetector, que monitora erros em serviços digitais.

Segundo a plataforma, houve um pico de cerca de 10 mil reclamações às 19h15. Os relatos de erros diminuíram por volta das 20h30.

Procurado pelo g1 , o Banco Central afirmou que "o PIX teve uma indisponibilidade parcial". Em nota, o órgão afirmou que "o problema foi rapidamente resolvido" por sua equipe técnica e que "os sistemas do Banco Central funcionam normalmente".

Os problemas mais relatados foram em aplicativos de celular, pagamentos e transferências .

No próprio Downdetector, alguns clientes especificaram bancos e reclamações. "Santander, Inter, Itaú fora do ar...", escreveu uma usuária. Outro diz que "C6, Mercado Livre, Itaú caiu tudo. Eu ainda consegui tranferir através do C6 Banking, mas caiu tb".

No X, o Itaú respondeu alguns internautas. O banco afirmou que estava ciente do problema. (Veja mais abaixo)

Outro cliente publicou uma foto da mensagem que está recebendo no aplicativo do banco:

O Bradesco fez o mesmo movimento. "Olá! Pedimos que tente acessar novamente mais tarde, por favor. Estamos à disposição", respondeu o banco em outra publicação.

Por enquanto, os bancos e fintechs mais citados são: Bradesco , Itaú , Santander , Nubank , Inter , C6 , Mercado Livre e 99Pay .

articles.title: Brasileiro com conta no banco Ueno consegue recuperar recursos | G1
articles.standfirst: Exportador gaúcho que mora em Assunção detalha impactos da intervenção na instituição financeira. Crise gerou desespero na população e levou à queda do presidente do país.
articles.summary: Exportador gaúcho que mora em Assunção detalha impactos da intervenção na instituição financeira. Crise gerou desespero na população e levou à queda do presidente do país.
articles.body:
Agência do Ueno Bank fechada em Pedro Juan Caballero. — Foto: Nádia Nicolau/TV Morena

Era uma terça-feira comum quando, nas primeiras horas da manhã, milhões de paraguaios acordam sem conseguir acessar suas contas no banco Ueno , um dos maiores do país . O Banco Central do Paraguai havia intervindo na instituição.

Poucas horas depois, o presidente do Banco Central renuncia. A população vai às ruas para se manifestar . Cerca de 48h depois, o presidente Santiago Peña pede renúncia enquanto o Congresso vota seu impeachment .

Esse é o relato do exportador de grãos gaúcho Pedro Bergallo, que mora há 7 anos no país vizinho e reside na capital Assunção .

"As pessoas se desesperaram. Foi um tumulto muito grande. As pessoas se dirigiram até a frente das agências e, quando chegaram, se depararam com uma carta colada nos vidros das agências com uma carta do Banco Central explicando o porquê do fechamento", conta.

Ele mesmo, que produz e industrializa arroz, milho e soja para exportação, possuía conta no Ueno e ficou sem ter acesso a parte de seus recursos . Cerca de dois dias depois, contudo, conseguiu recuperar.

"Eu tinha conta no Ueno, tinha um dinheiro que não era nada muito elevado, mas ficou retido e hoje (quinta-feira, 5) estou conseguindo a devolução desses fundos, assim como a maioria da população. Já pude recuperar o dinheiro que eu tinha no banco", afirma.

Pedro destaca que a crise impactou principalmente os mais pobres do país, e especialmente aqueles que tinham no Ueno o único lugar onde mantinham seu dinheiro.

" As pessoas passaram a entrar em desespero , principalmente quem não tinha plano B ou C em outras instituições financeiras. Teve muita gente de baixa renda que depositou sua confiança e seu dinheiro nesse banco ."

Na última semana, ele e os quase 6,5 milhões de habitantes do país estiveram envolvidos em um turbilhão de informações e reviravoltas de uma forma que ele afirma nunca ter vivido no Paraguai e nem no Brasil.

"Qual é o resultado prático da questão do banco Ueno? Oito diretores presos, o presidente da República impeachmado e o presidente do Banco Central fora também. Imagina: em apenas três dias a gente tem essa quantidade de acontecimentos."

A situação que culminou em uma das semanas mais politicamente intensas no Paraguai nas últimas décadas começou há cerca de dois anos.

" O Paraguai ainda tinha um mercado financeiro muito arcaico . Ainda usavam a TED, tu transferia às 8h e chegava ao meio-dia. Ainda se usava muito dinheiro físico. E veio o banco Ueno com uma ideia de um banco digital e nada mais", relata.

"Ele lança uma campanha massiva de criação de contas em 2024 e 2025. Começaram a liberar crédito com condições muito vantajosas. Muita gente usufruiu disso, inclusive eu . Tinha políticas de desconto muito efetivas em quase todas as lojas do país, posto de combustíveis, supermercado, shopping, cinema, tinham um desconto quase que inigualável em todas os estabelecimentos comerciais do país", complementa.

articles.title: Suze Orman challenges Americans to 'dig deep' and make 2 massive money moves in 2027 — and the payoff could be enormous
articles.summary: New responsibilities could gut your saving power, but all is not lost.
articles.body:
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.

Finance guru Suze Orman has some essential advice going into 2027.

In a LinkedIn post (1), the podcast host and best-selling author issued a challenge to all her readers, especially her younger audience.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

Gold has overtaken U.S. Treasuries as central banks' top reserve asset. Get Goldco's 2026 Precious Metals IRA Playbook for free

Specifically, Orman is challenging everyone to '"dig deep" and make two moves next year:

Increase your 401(k) savings rate by one or two percentage points.

Try to max out Roth IRA contributions if you are eligible to contribute.

Orman believes making these changes in the coming year matters for a few key reasons.

First, it may only get harder to save as time passes. You may face new responsibilities like being forced to step in as a caregiver for aging parents or to help your adult children. Or your career may not go as planned — with Orman citing AI as a major disruptor.

These obstacles, or other unforeseen events, could make it harder to increase your retirement account contributions, even if your career develops and income improves as you grow older.

Investing as much as you can, starting as early as you can, will leave you better positioned if life throws you curveballs.

Increasing your retirement investments next year could also have another benefit, according to Orman.

The sooner you start investing, the more compounding helps grow your wealth. Compounding happens when your returns can be reinvested and earn more money. If you're making 7% on your investments each year, putting that margin back into your portfolio can pay off massively 30 years later as you gear up to retire. It is a powerful force.

In fact, it is because of compounding that making a small change like increasing 401(k) contributions by 1% to 2% can make such an outsized difference.

Say, for example, that your household income is around $87,460 (2), which was the real median household income in 2025. If all of the earners in your household contributed an extra 1% of income, or around $874 starting in 2027 and kept that up for 25 years, the extra $874 in contributions would give you just about $86,000 in extra savings in retirement, assuming a 10% average annual ROI.

articles.title: Goldman’s US Stock Panic Gauge Hits Extreme, Signaling Rebound
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. traders said the violent selloff in US equities has pushed market panic to an extreme level that historically signals a strong rebou...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc. traders said the violent selloff in US equities has pushed market panic to an extreme level that historically signals a strong rebound over the medium term.

The bank's Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10 on Thursday, crossing the 9.5 threshold that marks the panic zone. The roughly five-point increase was the third-largest daily jump on record. Coming on the heels of a huge decline Wednesday, the fourth largest, it resulted in the biggest ever two-day swing, traders including Lee Coppersmith wrote.

"The combined two-day swing was the largest on record, which I think shows how quickly the market went from relief to outright panic," Coppersmith said.

The sharp reversal followed an aggressive wave of demand for downside protection ahead of Wednesday's US midterm vote. Clients had sold hedges into the post-election relief rally, leaving portfolios materially under-protected when equities turned lower. As stocks tumbled and forced liquidations spread across hedge funds, investors scrambled to buy back the protection they had just shed, according to the traders.

The rush for hedges was reflected in options activity. More than 11 million puts traded on Cboe on Thursday, the highest daily volume on record, surpassing the previous peak in April 2025. Index puts accounted for much of the activity, while single-stock put volume ranked fourth-highest ever, highlighting the concentration of demand in broad-market protection.

Still, Goldman's historical analysis suggests the medium-term outlook becomes more constructive when panic reaches such extremes. Following the 15 previous signals in which its Vol Panic Index exceeded 9.5, the S&P 500 gained an average 4.6% over the subsequent three months, with an 80% hit rate. Over six months, the average gain was 9%, with stocks rising in 73% of cases.

"Yesterday was as much about an exceptionally poor technical setup and forced re-hedging as it was about a deterioration in fundamentals," Coppersmith wrote.

While there is still more positioning to work through as markets continue to search for a bottom, the historical pattern suggests that extreme volatility and forced selling can eventually create opportunities for investors willing to look beyond the near-term turbulence, according to Goldman's traders.

articles.title: Market turmoil saps enthusiasm for the buzziest IPO of the year
articles.summary: Anthropic couldn’t have picked a worse time to pull off the biggest IPO the world has ever seen.
articles.body: Anthropic couldn’t have picked a worse time to pull off the biggest IPO the world has ever seen. Thursday marked one of the sharpest sell-offs on Wall Street in years. Tech stocks bore the brunt, but almost no equities were spared as fears of an AI slowdown gripped investors and sent them rushing to safety. The Nasdaq Composite lost $2.5 trillion in value, the biggest single-day dollar-value drop in its history. Asian and European markets followed the US down on Friday. Put simply: The vibes around AI have never been worse, and Anthropic — a company that seldom misses a chance to warn of doomsday scenarios — is trying to convince investors the future for AI has never been brighter. Thursday’s losses were so severe, some market commentators speculated that the company — which has been expected to make history this month with a target valuation of around $1.5 trillion — may have to delay the deal or significantly lower its price. Before Tuesday’s midterm elections, traders on the prediction market Kalshi had put the likelihood of Anthropic’s IPO taking place this month above 90% But on Thursday, as markets tumbled over fears the Democratic sweep would throttle the AI buildout, those odds fell to 60%. Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to CNN’s request for comment. “My view is that Anthropic can still come to market and will come to market [but] will likely be forced to do so at a lower valuation,” Mike O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, told CNN in an email. The market rout comes just days before Anthropic was expected to begin its pre-IPO “roadshow,” a process in which private companies try to stir up investor interest and gauge demand before pricing its shares. The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that three “major investors” who plan to participate in the IPO said the valuation would need to come down from the $1.5 trillion level analysts and investors have forecast. Investors have been awaiting Anthropic’s IPO in part because it is expected to serve as a barometer for not only the AI trade but the broader US economy, which has been buoyed by heavy investment in the data centers and energy infrastructure that Anthropic’s technology requires. At the same time, public sentiment around AI has been souring. Wall Street has been questioning whether companies may be overestimating the amount of demand they’ll see in the near future for AI. All of that was already weighing on AI-related stocks in the lead-up to Tuesday’s midterm elections. Markets rallied to historic highs on Wednesday after Democrats’ decisive win, followed by President Donald Trump’s comments that he would work with the opposition. But by Thursday, the reality of that Democratic sweep’s impact on AI settled in. Voters overwhelmingly elected candidates who are critical of data-center development — one of many potential pitfalls Anthropic warned about in its IPO prospectus last month. Even Dan Ives, one of the most bullish AI voices on Wall Street, struck a subdued note in an email to clients Thursday, saying he now expects the breakneck growth of Big Tech companies’ spending on AI to peak in 2027 rather than 2028 or 2029. “Our overall bullish tech thesis around the AI Revolution does not change, but it makes us more selective in the names and sectors that will outperform into 2027.” The political shift compounds an already complex financial picture for Anthropic. The AI company this week disclosed in an updated regulatory filing that it has committed to spending nearly $900 billion in the coming years on computing power and data centers — a staggering amount relative to the $132 billion in cash and investments the company was sitting on a month ago. “Many assumed the push for data center moratoriums was political theater that would fade after the election,” O’Rourke said in a note to clients Thursday. “This is no longer a bull-bear debate on AI infrastructure demand, there is clear evidence that a structural shift in the environment is underway.”

articles.title: Fox completes its $22B acquisition of Roku

articles.body:
Fox has completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, wrapping up one of the biggest media deals in recent years and giving the company a major boost in the streaming and connected TV space.

Announced Friday, the deal brings the streaming company founded in 2002 formally under Fox's ownership. Fox says the combined company now ranks as the third-largest television business in the U.S. by viewership.

"We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn't change today. What does change is our reach and resources," Roku founder Anthony Wood said in a statement. "Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us."

For Fox, the move provides direct access to Roku's reach of more than 100 million households. The company expects that audience to help it improve advertising targeting, strengthen its position in the fast-growing connected TV market, and reduce its reliance on traditional TV distribution.

Today's announcement comes two months after the Justice Department issued a second request for information, asking both companies to provide additional data and documents as part of its antitrust review. Earlier this month, reports suggested the deal was nearing U.S. regulatory approval.

The acquisition also closed much earlier than expected. When the deal was first announced in June, the companies projected it would be completed in the first half of 2027.

articles.title: Musk bids farewell to Cybertruck as Tesla bets on robots and self-driving
articles.summary: So long, Tesla Cybertruck; we hardly knew ye.
articles.body:
So long, Tesla ( TSLA ) Cybertruck, we hardly knew ye.

Yes, it is official. The Tesla Cybertruck will soon be no more, per a post from CEO Elon Musk on his X account.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote early Friday morning.

For many in the industry, this isn't a surprise even with Musk's grand pronouncements about the vehicle. Musk once boasted that Cybertruck demand was " so far off the hook, you can't even see the hook ," and the company said it had over 1 million preorders.

But conversion to sales never materialized. Cox Automotive's Kelley Blue Book estimated overall sales for the controversial pickup only hit around 71,000 since the vehicle went on sale in 2023. Tesla and Musk had built out capacity for Giga Austin to pump out 250K Cybertrucks per year; Tesla was selling about one-tenth that amount.

When the truck was first revealed in late 2019 , Musk had promised a sub-$40,000 price tag for the cheapest version, and up to 500 miles of range for the top-end model. None of these things materialized.

Tesla had wanted to get the first models out by late 2021, but delays in finalizing design, creating the large stainless steel body panels, and, of course, the pandemic delayed its release.

Now, after a near four-year run (by mid 2027), the Cybertruck is no more.

Musk and Tesla point to the need to boost production of the upcoming Cybercab, which has been testing in certain robotaxi markets. The Cybercab — which has no steering wheel or pedals — is a huge bet on autonomy and essentially ride-sharing as opposed to private ownership (though Tesla says the Cybercab will eventually go on sale to consumers).

The Cybertruck's discontinuation comes after the cancellation of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, two of Tesla's most significant — though pricey — models. At the time, Musk said the space at its Fremont factory where the S and X were made was needed for Optimus robot lines.

Now the EV truck space has a bit more clarity. Rivian's R1T pickup and GM's Chevrolet Silverado/GMC Sierra EV are now the only options; however, Ford will soon release the Fathom compact EV pickup . Then there's Slate , the startup with a no-frills, bare-bones $25K pickup.

Musk's soaring vision of Tesla as a robotics, software, and autonomy company is becoming clear. But many Tesla fans who enjoy driving their own vehicles may be concerned about what happens to the company's remaining EVs for sale — if the bet for Tesla is on tech rather than cars.

Pras Subramanian is the lead auto reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram .

articles.title: Medicare prescription drug costs could jump 50% next year. How to prepare.
articles.summary: Prescription drug expenses could climb next year. Here's what to review before your 2027 coverage begins.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

With about a month left before the Medicare open enrollment period ends on Dec. 7, millions of people with standalone Part D prescription drug plans face a 50% increase for 2027. KFF, a nonprofit health policy organization, estimates premiums will rise by an average of $17 a month.

But "averages hide the people who get hit hardest," said Ed Wu, physician and co-founder of Pinnie Health, a Medicare patient advocacy. "One of the biggest national plans goes from $126 to about $205 a month. That's close to $1,000 more a year for the same coverage. And the premium is only part of it."

The standard deductible is rising to $700, and the out-of-pocket cap rises from $2,100 to $2,400, Wu told Yahoo Finance — and more plans are moving from flat copays to coinsurance. "With coinsurance, the same brand-name prescription can cost a different amount from one month to the next."

Ultimately, patients are paying more up front, and those costs are getting harder to predict, he added.

Of the 10.4 million people in standalone prescription drug plans who face a premium increase, 2.4 million will see their monthly premium rise by $50 or more if they stay in the same plan for 2027, KFF reported. Last year, only 38,000 faced increases of that size.

"The biggest driver of the premium jump is due to the end of a federal program that had been holding down premiums for standalone Part D plans," Alexandra Robertson, chief growth officer at Visory Health, told Yahoo Finance.

Wu also noted that for the first time, zero-premium drug plans are being eliminated in 2027, "so more than 4 million people in $0 plans will have some tough choices to make."

He added that the cost dilemma is compounded by fewer options. "There are 316 standalone drug plans in 2027, down from 464 in 2025, about a third fewer in two years. The average person has 9 to pick from, down from 11."

The lowest- and highest-premium prescription drug plans

Monthly premiums vary widely, from about $6 to over $200. For example, an analysis by KFF identified national prescription drug plans with the lowest and highest average premiums.

Centene's Wellcare Value Script Rx, an enhanced PDP with an average premium of $6.50 for 2027 (up from $5.80 in 2026)

Wellcare Classic, a basic PDP with an average premium of $10.90 for 2027 (up from $8.60 in 2026.

United's AARP Medicare Rx Preferred ($204.50, up from $126 in 2026)

Humana Premier Rx Plan ($137.40, up from $119.60 in 2026)

KFF estimates that 65% of Medicare beneficiaries did not compare their Medicare coverage options during last year's open enrollment period.

"Don't let your plan renew without looking at it," Robertson said. "Plans can change every year, and especially with plan increases coming in 2027, it makes sense to take a good look at the premium, the deductible, which drugs are covered, and which pharmacies are in your network."

Medicare beneficiaries receive an Annual Notice of Change that shows what's different for next year. Make sure to review that and compare it to all the medications you currently take, she added.

The single most important thing is to shop before Dec. 7. If you do nothing, you're accepting whatever your plan charges, Wu said, offering these suggestions:

Put your actual drug list into Medicare's Plan Finder on Medicare.gov and compare the total yearly cost: premium, deductible, and what you'll pay for your drugs. A cheap premium is no bargain if your blood thinner sits on an expensive tier. Plans in the same state run from about $5 to over $200 a month — a huge spread.

Check with your doctor . Often, your doctor doesn't know how much you're paying, and they might be able to find suitable, lower-cost alternatives. This may take an extra visit or two if a new medication is involved, but it can lead to a lower-cost medication. Sometimes, if a drug you need isn't covered, your doctor can request an exception.

If money is tight, apply for Extra Help through Social Security. It can bring premiums and copays down to a few dollars, and many people who qualify never apply.

Ask about the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan if your costs come in big chunks early in the year. It spreads your out-of-pocket costs into monthly payments.

Robertson also reminds Medicare beneficiaries to look into free prescription savings cards.

"For some drugs like generics, the discount card price can be lower than your plan copay. It's worth asking the pharmacist to compare the two before you check out," she said. "One thing to keep in mind is that you can't use an Rx discount card with your insurance, but you can use it instead of your insurance."

What to do if your prescription becomes unaffordable

"As a physician, I worry less about the premium than about what people do when costs jump: they skip doses, split pills, or stop filling a prescription — and that's how a manageable condition turns into an ER visit," Wu said.

If a drug becomes unaffordable, Wu recommends calling your doctor or working with an advocate before you stop taking it.

articles.title: 55-year-old sandwich chain operator files Chapter 11 bankruptcy
articles.summary: The Texas-based Schlotzsky’s Deli franchisee faces declining revenue.
articles.body:
The sandwich dining sector is a competitive market, with franchisees of various chains, such as Schlotzsky's, battling the industry leader Subway for market share.

Subway has had its share of problems, as the chain finished 2025 with 729 fewer locations, totaling 18,773.

Schlotzsky's has closed locations in 2026 but has not revealed a list of those restaurants. Its franchisees have also filed for bankruptcy protection to reorganize their businesses, which includes closing locations and rejecting leases.

Schlotzky's franchisee files for bankuptcy

Schlotzsky's Deli franchisee JPrieto Hospitality LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after facing a severe decline in revenue in 2026, compared to the two previous years.

The San Antonio, Texas-based franchisee, which operated 10 Schlotzsky's locations in North Texas in early 2026, filed its petition on Nov. 5 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Texas, listing over $532,000 in assets and $350,000 in liabilities.

JPrieto's annual revenue has declined from $8.26 million in 2024 to $8.19 million in 2025, before falling to $4.11 million in 2026 until Nov. 5 when it filed for bankruptcy, according to the petition.

The debtor's largest unsecured creditors include Schlotzsky's franchisor GoToFoods . which it owes over $148,000; food and beverage supplier Ben. E. Keith, owed $35,000; TCR Heating & Air LLC, owed over $19,000; Cooling Equipment Specialist LLC, owed over $18,000; and produce supplier Brothers Food Service, owed $15,000.

Schlotzsky's was founded in Austin, Texas, in 1971 and operates about 280 restaurants in 25 states.

In addition to Schlotzsky's, franchisor GoToFoods' brands include Jamba, Auntie Anne's, Cinnabon, Moe's Southwest Grill, McAlister's Deli, and Carvel ice cream shops. GoToFoods is affiliated with Roark Capital Group.

JPrieto Hospitality operated 10 Schlotzsky's locations on March 31, 2026, according to a Franchise Disclosure Document provided by GetFDD . The franchisee listed five current Texas leases in its petition, including two in Fort Worth; and one each in North Mansfield, Grand Prairie, and Cedar Hill, Texas.

The debtor's petition also listed lease terminations in Weatherford, Hudson, and Granbury, Texas. The petition did not indicate if JPrieto is operating more than the five locations identified in the filing.

Other sandwich chain operators have had a difficult year in 2026, including Subway sandwich chain franchisee MTF Enterprises LLC , which began the year filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Jan. 21, 2026, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

articles.title: JetBlue hikes checked-bag fees to as much as $70, costing a family of four up to $680 round-trip over the holidays
articles.summary: Even if the price of jet fuel drops, airline travel isn’t suddenly going to get cheaper. Here’s why — and how to save.
articles.body:
Planning to travel this Thanksgiving? Be prepared to fork over more cash for your checked bags.

Many airlines increased their checked bag fees back in March, following the outbreak of the war in Iran, when jet fuel prices skyrocketed. Now, JetBlue is doing it again.

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

With its latest round of price increases, you could pay up to $140 for a round-trip flight for a single bag. The fees, which are now in effect, apply to domestic flights, as well as flights to Canada, Latin America, the Caribbean and some Transatlantic destinations.

As airlines continue to struggle with higher operating expenses, we likely won't see the cost of travel come down any time soon.

JetBlue's new prices reflect peak and off-peak travel. So if you're traveling during Thanksgiving (Nov 19-30) or Christmas (Dec. 17 - Jan. 18), expect to pay more.

If you pay your checked-bag fee more than 24 hours in advance, it costs $50 for the first bag — that's up from the previous $39 — or $55 during peak travel for a one-way basic fare. If you pay less than 24 hours before you fly, then the cost is even higher: $60 (off-peak) and $70 (peak).

Checking a second bag? In advance, you'll pay $70 one way (off-peak) and $75 (peak). Less than 24 hours ahead of your flight, you'll pay $75 one way (off-peak) and $85 (peak). A third bag comes in at a flat $200.

It's gotten so complicated that there's a chart to consult , showing the checked-bag fees based on your fare class, origin, destination, travel dates and status with the airline.

But it boils down to this: A family of four checking one bag each at the airport over the holidays will pay $680 round-trip just for their bags. Once you add in seat selection, for-purchase meals and snacks and, in some cases, fuel surcharges, the cost of a trip might be more than you were budgeting for.

The rising cost of jet fuel is just one of many factors impacting carriers' operating costs. That means, even if the price of jet fuel drops, airline travel isn't suddenly going to get cheaper.

articles.title: Stocks had their worst day in 18 months — here's what that means for your portfolio
articles.summary: Thursday's stock sell-off was mostly an AI story: Chip stocks crashed, while the typical stock in the S&P 500 is barely off its high.
articles.body:
The AI trade ran off a cliff Thursday. Most of the stock market was nowhere near the edge.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell more than 4% Thursday, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. About $3 trillion in stock market value disappeared in a single session.

Chipmakers took the hardest hit. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) dropped 12%, its worst day since March 2020, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 9% , its worst day since the DeepSeek scare in January 2025.

The trigger was Washington. Democrats won control of Congress this week, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers, the giant buildings those chips go into. Investors worry that new rules could slow the building boom that sent chip stocks to records.

But look past the AI stocks, and the picture gets a lot calmer.

The S&P 500 is only about 5% below its October record and is still up about 8% this year. The typical stock in the index is about 3% off its high, and more than half of S&P 500 stocks are up for the week.

How can both be true? The S&P 500 gives the biggest companies the biggest say. Chipmakers alone make up about 14% of the index, by Yahoo Finance's count, so when they crash, they drag the whole index down even when most other companies are holding steady.

For an average portfolio, the damage so far is modest. For every $1,000 in an S&P 500 index fund at the market's Oct. 6 peak, you'd have about $950 left, and the index is still up about 8% this year. Savers in target-date funds, which mix stocks with bonds, fared even better Thursday. Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund ( VTTHX ) lost less than 3%, compared with more than 4% for the S&P 500.

Stocks are bouncing Friday, with chip stocks leading the way, after a strong jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the roughly 70,000 economists expected.

One good day doesn't mean the danger has passed.

The same setup that cushioned investors this week cuts both ways. AI-linked companies are a big piece of the S&P 500, and they've powered much of the market's gains in recent years. If the AI slide deepens, index funds like those based on the S&P 500 will feel it a lot more.

Rich Bernstein, global head of macro and customized investing at Janus Henderson Investors, compared the AI run to Wile E. Coyote , the cartoon character forever chasing the Road Runner off cliffs.

"You're running full speed, and then you realize that there's nothing anymore, and you fall to the bottom of the canyon," Bernstein said on Yahoo Finance's "Market Domination" on Thursday. "That's momentum investing."

articles.title: What the AI stock crash cost your 401(k) for every $1,000 invested
articles.summary: Thursday's AI stock crash cost a basic S&P 500 index fund about a nickel on the dollar, while chip stocks lost nearly a third of their value.
articles.body:
AI stocks just had their worst crash in years. If your 401(k) sits in a basic index fund, you lost about a nickel on the dollar.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell more than 4% on Thursday, its worst day in more than a year and a half , as chip stocks had their worst day since the beginning of the pandemic in March 2020. Nvidia ( NVDA ) had its worst day since the DeepSeek scare in January 2025.

Here's what that looks like in dollars: For every $1,000 invested in an S&P 500 index fund at the market's Oct. 6 peak, you'd have about $950 today. The same $1,000 in chip stocks would be worth about $710, and in Nvidia, about $790.

If your fund tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ), the damage is closer to a dime on the dollar. The index closed Thursday in a correction — Wall Street's term for a drop of 10% or more from a record.

Meanwhile, the typical stock in the S&P 500 is actually up a little since that peak.

How? The S&P 500 gives the biggest companies the biggest say. Chipmakers alone make up about 14% of the index, by Yahoo Finance's count. When they crash, the hundreds of other companies in the fund help cushion the blow.

Stocks are bouncing Friday after a strong jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double what economists expected.

But that cushion cuts both ways. AI-linked companies are a big slice of most index funds, and they've powered much of the market's gains in recent years. If the AI slide deepens, your 401(k) will feel it a lot more.

The worry stems from the data centers that run on those chips. Democrats won control of Congress this week, and candidates in both parties campaigned against them. The market rout reflects "uncertainty about the cost and pace of the data center buildout," Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, wrote in a note Thursday.

History offers some comfort — with an asterisk. The S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after every midterm election since 1950 — a track record of 19 for 19 — according to Yahoo Finance calculations. But that's only 19 cases, and none came with an AI boom this big on the line. Thursday may also be a warning sign: It was the Dow Jones Industrial Average's ( ^DJI ) worst second day after a midterm in data going back to 1896.

Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, has a simple message for nervous investors.

"Don't freak out. Just keep your head about you," Sosnick said on Yahoo Finance's "The 8:30" on Friday. "There's reasons to sell. There's reasons to buy."

articles.title: IRS announces 2027 income tax brackets. Here's what's changing.
articles.summary: Find out how much you'll owe when you file your 2026 and 2027 tax returns, and learn how to pay less by reducing your taxable income.
articles.body:
Your tax rate is the percentage of income you pay in taxes, but it isn't the same for all the money you earn. Different portions of the income you earn are taxed at specific rates called tax brackets. Every year, the Internal Revenue Service makes annual adjustments to account for inflation.

The IRS announced the 2027 annual inflation adjustments for taxpayers, including increases across all seven federal tax brackets, as well as increases to the maximum capital gains rate, estate tax exclusions, and the child tax credit.

For 2027, the top tax rate remains 37% for single filers with incomes above $661,375 or $793,650 for married couples filing jointly. The other rates are: 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, and 35%.

These income brackets apply to tax returns filed in 2028.

The U.S. has a progressive tax system. That means that as your income rises, the total individual income tax you pay is also supposed to increase.

Because Americans with higher incomes are taxed at a higher rate, some taxpayers worry that getting a pay raise will put them in a higher tax bracket. However, this concern reflects a common misconception about how tax brackets and tax rates work.

There are two basic types of tax rates: marginal and effective .

Marginal tax rate: Your marginal tax rate is the percentage of income tax you owe on the last dollar earned.

Effective tax rate: The percentage of your income that you actually pay to the IRS in taxes.

Your marginal tax rate is different from your effective tax rate because your income is taxed at different rates. Think of tax brackets as a series of buckets. When one bucket reaches the tipping point, the extra amount flows over into the next.

For example, suppose you're a single taxpayer who has taxable income of $40,000 in 2027. As you can see from the federal income tax brackets, your marginal tax rate would be 12%.

Calculating your effective tax rate is a little more complicated. Here's how your income would be taxed according to 2027 brackets:

You'd owe 10% in taxes on the first $12,800 you earned, or $1,280.

You'd owe 12% in taxes on the next 27,200 (40,000-$12,800) you earned, or $3,264.

Your total tax bill would be $4,544. Since your total income is $40,000, your effective tax rate is 11.36%.

Now imagine your boss gives you a $15,000 pay raise, bringing your income to $55,000. Your marginal rate would shoot up to 22%, which sounds like a pretty steep hike. But since different portions of your income are taxed at different rates, the impact isn't so bad. Here's how your tax bill would break down:

You'd owe 12% in taxes on the next $39,225 ($52,025-$12,800) you earned, or about $4,707.

You'd owe 22% in taxes on the remaining $2,975 ($55,000-$52,025) you earned, or about $654.50.

Your total tax liability is $6,641.50, which is an effective tax rate of about 12.08%. Even though you're in a higher tax bracket, your effective tax rate increases only slightly because a small portion of your income is subject to the higher tax rate.

Of course, the example above is a bit oversimplified because federal income taxes aren't the only taxes you pay. Most people pay the first 7.65% of their income toward Social Security and Medicare taxes — or 15.3% if you're self-employed. It also doesn't account for state and local taxes, sales taxes, or property taxes.

But the bottom line is, even if you're pushed into a higher federal tax bracket, it's not a bad thing. You may owe more in taxes, but you'll get even more extra money in your paycheck.

How to get into a lower bracket and reduce your taxes

No one likes paying taxes, so you generally want your taxable income to be as low as possible. Here are some steps you can take to lower your tax liability.

Weigh the standard deduction vs. itemized deductions

When you file your taxes, you'll need to figure out whether the standard deduction or itemized deductions will provide a larger reduction to your taxable income.

The standard deduction is $16,600 for single filers, $33,200 if you're married filing jointly, and $24,925 for heads of households in tax year 2027. If you opt for the standard deduction, you can subtract the full deduction for your tax filing status from your taxable income.

But itemizing could yield greater tax savings if you paid substantial mortgage interest, made large charitable contributions, or had unreimbursed medical expenses exceeding 7.5% of your adjusted gross income.

Consult with a tax professional to determine which option is best for your situation.

You can lower your taxable income if you contribute to a workplace retirement account like a 401(k) or 403(b).

Note that only contributions to pre-tax accounts will reduce your taxes, and withdrawals will be taxed as ordinary income later on. If you contribute to a Roth account, you won't get a tax break for the current year, but you can take tax-free withdrawals in retirement.

A tax deduction lowers your taxable income. Some tax deductions are known as above-the-line deductions, which means you can take them even if you don't itemize your return. Some common above-the-line deductions you can take include:

Traditional IRA contributions: You may be able to deduct contributions to a traditional IRA , though income thresholds apply if you or your spouse are covered by a retirement plan at work. You have until Tax Day to fund an IRA for any given tax year, so funding a traditional IRA before April 15, 2027, could lower your 2026 tax bill.

Student loan interest: If you paid interest on your student loans , you can deduct up to $2,500 of interest payments, though income limits apply.

Health savings account (HSA) contributions: You can deduct HSA contributions even if you don't itemize your return. Your withdrawals will never be taxable either, as long as you use them for qualifying medical expenses. As with IRA contributions, you can make a contribution until Tax Day, so you can still make 2026 HSA contributions up until April 15, 2027.

If you're self-employed, you may be eligible for additional tax deductions for small business owners .

Tax credits are even more valuable than tax deductions because they reduce the amount you owe in taxes dollar-for-dollar. If the credit is refundable, you can get any amount that exceeds your tax liability as a tax refund. Here are some popular tax credits you could qualify for this upcoming tax season:

Child tax credit: For 2026, the child tax credit is worth up to $2,200 per qualifying dependent child under age 17. There's a refundable portion of the credit called the additional child tax credit that's worth up to $1,700. That increases to $2,300, with $1,800 refundable in 2027.

Child and dependent care credit: If you paid someone to care for your child younger than 13 or a qualifying tax dependent who was unable to care for themselves — and you needed to do so because you were working or looking for work — you could qualify for the child and dependent care credit . The credit is worth between 20% and 50% of your expenses, with a cap of $3,000 for one dependent or $6,000 for two or more dependents.

Earned income tax credit: The earned income tax credit (EITC) provides a tax break to lower- and middle-income families who earned money from working during the year. The maximum value for the 2026 tax year ranges from $664 for those with no qualifying children to $8,231 for families with three or more qualifying children.

Education tax credits: If you paid for higher education expenses for yourself or your dependent, you may be able to take one of two education tax credits : the American Opportunity Tax Credit, worth up to $2,500 per qualifying student, or the Lifetime Learning Credit, worth up to $2,000 per income tax return. You can claim both on the same return, but you can only claim one for the same student or expense.

Saver's credit: The saver's credit is available to low- and middle-income workers who save for their retirement in an account like a 401(k) or an IRA. The maximum credit is $1,000 for single filers or $2,000 for married couples filing jointly.

What tax bracket am I in? How to figure it out.

To figure out what tax bracket you're in, you'll need to know your tax filing status and your taxable income . If you have a traditional job, your starting place for calculating your taxable income is to look at Box 1 of your W-2. If you're self-employed, you'll need to look at the Forms 1099-NEC you've received. You may need to account for other sources of taxable income, like interest, capital gains, or Social Security.

Once you know your taxable income, look at the IRS tax bracket charts to see which range your income falls into. Your tax bracket is your marginal tax rate, or the rate you're taxed on the last dollar you earned. But your effective tax rate, or the percentage of income you pay in taxes, will be lower because your income is taxed at different rates that gradually get higher as you earn more.

Note that you won't be able to calculate your tax brackets for 2026 or 2027 until you've received all your tax forms for either year. Employers are required to send W-2 forms by Jan. 31 for the previous year, so you'll have the numbers you need to calculate your 2026 tax bracket around Jan. 31, 2027. But you may be able to use a recent pay stub to estimate your taxable income and tax bracket.

Is taxable income the same as gross income?

No, but gross income is the starting point for determining taxable income . You take your gross income and subtract any above-the-line deductions, like pre-tax retirement contributions and student loan payments, to arrive at your adjusted gross income. Then, you apply either the standard deduction or your itemized deduction, which gives you your taxable income.

To get in a lower tax bracket, contribute as much as you can to tax-advantaged accounts like 401(k)s, IRAs, and HSAs, and look for any tax deductions and credits you may qualify for. Check with your tax preparer about whether you'll save more from itemizing or claiming the standard deduction.

articles.title: OpenAI to press ahead with data-center expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO tells CNBC
articles.summary: Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-center expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fueled fears of tight...
articles.body:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-center expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fueled fears of tighter scrutiny of the facilities, its Chief Financial Officer Sarah ‌Friar told CNBC in an interview on Friday.

"When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking ‌about how do we keep investing to meet customer demand," Friar said. "We are going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can ​get the compute we need," she added.

One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry's growth. It launched a charm offensive on Thursday to win over communities as opposition to data centers becomes a rallying point for anxieties about the technology.

As part of the efforts, OpenAI said, it ‌will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with ⁠public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites. It will also give residents access to construction plans and their potential effects.

Growing data-center opposition was a crucial issue in the midterm elections. Democratic ⁠candidates, including Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, made tighter scrutiny of the facilities a central campaign pledge. The Lone Star State is one of the fastest-growing data-center regions in the world.

Fears the Democratic sweep may slow construction of the facilities critical to the AI boom wiped ​about $2.5 ​trillion off the US stock market on Thursday, as investors weighed ​the fallout for the chip, cloud and networking industries ‌that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the spending frenzy.

Still, there are signs that tech giants remain committed to data-center expansion plans despite the growing backlash.

Alphabet-owned Google said on Thursday it would invest $17 billion to build its first data center in Wyoming.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance is considering expanding a data center project in northeastern Brazil, a move that would strengthen its standing as Latin America's leading builder of computing facilities.

Friar also told CNBC that OpenAI was raising ‌fresh capital, pushing back against suggestions the ChatGPT maker had scaled back ​its fundraising ambitions amid the sharp AI stocks selloff.

The company is seeking ​fresh capital after its business grew 70% quarter over ​quarter in the third quarter, with enterprise demand doubling over the same period, she said.

articles.title: Gregorio Jiménez se alía con grandes fortunas nacionales y recupera el control de Burger King España por 2.330 millones
articles.standfirst: El empresario ha cerrado un acuerdo para comprar la participación mayoritaria del fondo británico Cinven
articles.summary: El empresario ha cerrado un acuerdo para comprar la participación mayoritaria del fondo británico Cinven
articles.body: Gregorio Jiménez, presidente y fundador de Restaurant Brands Europe (RBE) –la compañía que gestiona Burger King, Popeyes y Tim Hortons en España, Portugal e Italia– ha cerrado un acuerdo definitivo para comprar la participación mayoritaria del fondo británico Cinven en una operación valorada en 2.330 millones de euros. Esta transacción se consolida como la mayor operación de la historia en el sector de la restauración en España. "Esta operación representa un paso natural en la evolución de Restaurant Brands Europe y reafirma mi compromiso con el proyecto", ha señalado el empresario en el comunicado, subrayando que afrontan la nueva etapa "con una visión de largo plazo". Por su parte, el consejero delegado de RBE, Borja Hernández de Alba, ha destacado que los últimos años han sido "un periodo de enorme transformación y crecimiento". La nueva configuración del capital divide el control de la compañía en un bloque mayoritario (51%) y socios minoritarios y matriz (49%). El primero está encabezado por Gregorio Jiménez (20%), junto a la familia Costa (Costa Food Group, con más del 15% tras aportar 100 millones) y la familia Galán (vía family office Royal Park, con cerca del 15% tras invertir 80 millones). El segundo grupo está integrado por los fondos Point Break Capital Management y RAM, Fernando Núñez (Grupo Ibérica), Santiago Jiménez, el equipo directivo y la matriz estadounidense Restaurant Brands International (RBI) con más del 10%. Para acometer la operación, se ha cerrado un préstamo de 1.400 millones liderado por Banco Santander, junto a J.P. Morgan y BBVA. Como asesores financieros actuaron Santander CIB y J.P. Morgan (con A&O Shearman en la parte legal), mientras que Cinven contó con Morgan Stanley y Clifford Chance. El equipo directivo se mantendrá con Gregorio Jiménez al frente y Borja Hernández de Alba como consejero delegado. Tras el ciclo de Cinven (que elevó las ventas de RBE a 1.541 millones y el EBITDA a 245 millones en 2025), el gran objetivo del nuevo consorcio tras el cierre previsto para el primer trimestre de 2027 será integrar por completo Burger King Italia.

articles.title: Supreme Court to Hear Goldman Sachs’ Bankruptcy Arbitration Bid
articles.summary: The US Supreme Court agreed to review a request by Goldman Sachs on whether bankruptcy courts can override arbitration agreements, setting up a high-stakes t...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg Law) -- The US Supreme Court agreed to review a request by Goldman Sachs on whether bankruptcy courts can override arbitration agreements, setting up a high-stakes test of the Federal Arbitration Act's reach.

The court on Friday approved the multinational investment bank's request that the high court clarify whether, and under what circumstances, a bankruptcy court can refuse to enforce an arbitration agreement for claims under Section 362(k) of US Bankruptcy Code if a creditor violates the automatic litigation stay protecting bankrupt people and companies.

Goldman Sachs said that because Section 362(k) issues arise frequently in bankruptcy, a circuit split on this issue reflected lower-court confusion about the FAA's intersection with bankruptcy law.

Goldman Sachs lost a bid in the US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit to compel arbitration in a suit alleging it violated bankruptcy law by continuing debt collection efforts despite the stay. The majority of the three-judge Fourth Circuit panel found that arbitration inherently conflicts with the core purposes of the bankruptcy code. Judge Robert B. King, in a dissent, found that the debtors' claims belong in arbitration.

The FAA creates a national policy favoring arbitration when parties have agreed to it. But bankruptcy law is designed to provide a collective, centralized resolution of a debtor's financial affairs. Courts are generally divided over the use of a test that considers whether issues are "core" or "non-core" and whether arbitration creates an inherent conflict.

The Supreme Court hasn't tested the tension between the two statutory schemes. The debtors in this lawsuit, two holders of Apple Card accounts issued by Goldman Sachs, argued the Supreme Court shouldn't take the case because its specific facts — involving a Chapter 13 stay — make it an unsuitable fit to properly resolve the broader legal question.

The American Bankers Association filed an amicus brief in support of Goldman Sachs.

Latham & Watkins LLP represents Goldman Sachs. Kellett & Bartholow PLLC and Giles & Lambert PC represent the consumer borrowers.

The case is Goldman Sachs Bank USA v. Brown, U.S., No. 25-1408, cert denied/granted 11/6/26.

articles.title: These 4 Trump-backed chip stocks have seen steeper losses than the beleaguered sector
articles.summary: Intel and three other government-backed semiconductor companies have seen price declines that have outpaced the beleaguered sector as a whole.
articles.body:
Chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) is putting a notable drag on the burgeoning US government investment portfolio, shaving close to $20 billion off the government's stake in the chipmaker.

But it's not the only one. The Trump administration's other semiconductor investments have also incurred sharp losses that outpace the beleaguered sector.

Chipmaker GlobalFoundries ( GFS ), photonics company Aeluma ( ALMU ), and silicon carbide specialist Wolfspeed ( WOLF ) have all seen losses of at least 40% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.

That's in excess of PHLX Semiconductor ( ^SOX ), a capitalization-weighted index of the semiconductor sector, which is down about over 18% over the same span.

The government's portfolio, which spans 41 companies and includes industries from critical minerals to drones, according to a CATO Institute tracker , has taken investors on a wild ride since the Trump administration started buying up stakes last year.

Semiconductor stocks have proved especially volatile, with sharper ups and downs, including a bounceback in evidence Friday . All four were up more than 5% at midday, and some by double digits, as the sector as a whole jumped a more modest 4%.

The price action in these public chipmakers doesn't capture the private companies that have also negotiated equity stakes with the US government.

Trump and his team have placed extra focus on semiconductors, leveraging funds made available by the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act to acquire equity stakes in a host of private chipmakers, including Commonwealth Fusion Systems and xLight.

The Trump administration has also negotiated stakes in quantum computing companies using CHIPS Act money that have similarly struggled amid headwinds facing the tech sector as a whole.

The government portfolio of quantum computing companies includes publicly traded companies like D-Wave Quantum ( QBTS ), Infleqtion ( INFQ ), Quantinuum ( QNT ), and Rigetti Computing ( RGTI ).

The price oscillations could give ammunition to critics of the administration's investing approach. Economic research shows that full or partial government ownership in companies has historically led to worse outcomes for the companies and their stakeholders.

In a 2025 survey of economists , a large majority said that a government taking equity stakes tends to be detrimental to both a company's performance and its governance standards.

The mixed results of the government's investments at the moment also fly in the face of the outsized returns for taxpayers that Trump and his team often promise.

articles.summary: El precio de la luz se abarató este sábado

A medida que avanza el día, es crucial prestar atención a las horas más caras y más baratas para optimizar el gasto energético. Los precios de la luz alcanzan sus máximos entre las 17:00 y las 22:00, donde se concentra el bloque más caro de horas. Además, se observan tramos elevados de precios, como las horas entre las 18:00 y 21:00, que se mantienen por encima de los 275 €/MWh, lo que refleja la alta demanda energética en estos momentos del día. La luz es más barata durante la madrugada y las primeras horas de la mañana, lo que presenta una clara oportunidad de ahorro para los consumidores. Las franjas horarias destacadas son 02:00 - 03:00, 236.18 €/MWh y 03:00 - 04:00, 229.76 €/MWh, donde se observan los precios más bajos, alcanzando mínimos de 226.75 €/MWh entre las 04:00 - 05:00 y 05:00 - 06:00. En este análisis, se destaca una notoria concentración de precios elevados durante la tarde y la noche, lo que invita a los consumidores a reflexionar sobre sus hábitos de consumo energético. Estas fluctuaciones significativas en el costo de la electricidad pueden influir de manera directa en la factura mensual, haciendo que una gestión más consciente del uso de energía se vuelva esencial para optimizar gastos.
